title: getQueryState
subtitle: Get complete query state
description: Synchronously get the complete state of a query including data, loading status, error, and metadata.

rows.name: queryKey
rows.description: Unique identifier for the query. Can be a string or array of primitives.

rows.name: options
rows.description: Optional configuration object. If no fetcher is provided, uses a previously registered fetcher.

returns.description: The complete query state. Always returns a state object, creating one if it doesn't exist.

examples.title: Basic Usage
Conditional Operations
examples.description: Use query state for conditional operations

behavior.title: Complete State
behavior.description: Returns all query state including data, loading, error, and metadata

behavior.title: Synchronous
behavior.description: Returns state immediately without waiting for network requests

behavior.title: No Side Effects
behavior.description: Does not trigger fetches or subscriptions

behavior.title: Type Safe
behavior.description: Returns properly typed state or undefined

dos: Use for conditional logic based on complete query state
Use in event handlers and non-React code
Check multiple state properties for comprehensive logic
donts: Don't use in render functions (use useQuery instead)
Don't assume state will always be available
Don't use for data that must be fresh
Don't forget to handle all possible state combinations

callouts.title: Complete State Access
callouts.content: getQueryState provides access to the complete query state, including loading status, errors, and metadata.
